user_direction: Commercial DVD playback is the performance target; validate the maximum DVD bitrate rather than requiring the 18.65 Mbps stress file to run at nominal cadence.

engineering_targets.scope: SD DVD-Video, not HD DVD or Blu-ray; combined budget includes video, audio, subpictures and system overhead, not an additional allocation on top of video.

source_review.project_reference_status: DVD_VIDEO is deferred to authorized DVD FLLC Part 2 and Part 3 books; generic H.262/H.222 do not establish DVD application constraints.

supporting_primary_vendor_source.document: A DVD Primer / DVD入門, Japanese edition, updated March 2004
supporting_primary_vendor_source.section: DVD-Video Basics, CBR/VBR and DVD bandwidth calculation
supporting_primary_vendor_source.verified_summary: Maximum video rate 9.8 Mbps; maximum combined DVD-Video rate 10.08 Mbps.
supporting_primary_vendor_source.authority_limit: Primary authoring-vendor guidance, not a replacement for the controlled DVD application books or a formal conformance certificate.

existing_evidence.entry591: Qualified warm 8 Mbps fixture passes full completion, zero errors and zero post-startup deadline misses; this is not maximum-rate validation.
existing_evidence.entry590: 18.646387 Mbps average video stress fixture remains late despite substantial improvement; retained as optional diagnostic evidence, not a DVD acceptance gate.

next_validation: Prepare a deterministic 9.8 Mbps video fixture in the currently supported picture subset, on GUNSMOKE, with measured bitrate and VBV/header/decode checks; a requested encoder rate or whole-file average alone is insufficient evidence.
Verify full-rate playback, zero errors/deadline misses, guarded transport integrity, startup, warm loads and menu responsiveness on hardware; retain user control of reboot/core load/playback.

Qualify a combined stream at the 10.08 Mbps budget with supported audio and timing when that feature boundary is ready; include actual internal framing and decoded PCM traffic in the helper-to-FPGA budget.

Extend coverage to required I/P/B and field-picture/DCT behavior, NTSC/PAL and film cadence, audio/PTS and disc navigation through their feature milestones; bitrate success alone does not establish commercial-disc compatibility.
restrictions: Do not treat compressed DVD input rate as a maximum physical HPS-to-FPGA rate; protocol overhead and expanded audio can add internal traffic.
Do not equate maximum average bitrate with worst decoder work or ignore legal buffering/bursts.
Do not continue production optimization solely to make the out-of-scope 18.65 Mbps fixture pass.
Preserve credit/integrity guards, FIFO sizes, startup, continuous HDMI sync and black idle; propose a bounded production revision only if in-scope evidence requires one.
